knowledgePattern: Rename logarithms to solve linked linear and quadratic conditions

hints.title: Rename the repeated logarithms
hints.body: Introduce one variable for each base-2 logarithm. Use logarithm laws to rewrite the first two conditions.
hints.recap: Product and power laws turn logarithms of products into linear combinations.
hints.pitfall: A product of two logarithms is not the logarithm of a product.
hints.pause: Write the three equations in the new variables.

recall.reminder: Product and power laws turn logarithms of products into linear combinations.

hints.title: Eliminate before solving
hints.body: Use the simpler linear equation in the other linear equation, so that the product condition contains just one unknown.
hints.recap: Substitution links equations that must hold for the same unknowns.
hints.pitfall: The values of the logarithmic variable are not yet the requested original values.
hints.pause: Solve the resulting equation, undo the substitution and check the domain.

recall.reminder: Substitution links equations that must hold for the same unknowns.

solution:
1. The logarithms require z>0, as well as the given x,y>0. Put X=log2x, Y=log2y, Z=log2z. The equations become 2X+Y+Z=3, X+Z=1, and YZ=2.

2. From X=1−Z, the first equation gives Y=1+Z. Hence Z(Z+1)=2, so (Z+2)(Z−1)=0.

3. For Z=1, we have (x,y,z)=(1,4,2). For Z=−2, we have (x,y,z)=(8,1/2,1/4). Both triples satisfy all domain restrictions.

4. The required sum is 2+1/4=9/4. Answer B.
